This is a test post to confirm that R chunks run and plots render.

## The data

The built-in `mtcars` dataset has fuel economy and design figures for 32 cars.

### Summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: summary
data(mtcars)
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")])
```

### Correlations

```{r}
#| label: cor
round(cor(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp")]), 2)
```

## A plot

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg-wt
#| fig-cap: "Fuel economy falls as vehicle weight rises."
#| warning: false
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(colour = "#3c5c3a", size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "#a86f1a", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## A simple model

```{r}
#| label: model
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
summary(fit)$coefficients
```

## Wrapping up

If you can see the code, its output, and the plot above, Quarto and R are wired up correctly.
